blocks.text: 11. Justice
The Blade of Truth
Numbered eleven, Justice sits upon a stone throne, holding a sword in her right hand and scales in her left.
Unlike the fluctuating Wheel of Fortune, she represents the unshakeable law of cause and effect.
She is the archetype of intellectual clarity, cutting through confusion with the razor-sharp edge of truth.
Her gaze is direct and piercing, signifying that nothing can be hidden from the eyes of cosmic law.
The Scales of Equilibrium
In her left hand, she balances the golden scales.
These represent intuition and the weighing of evidence.
Before she strikes with the sword of action, she must first measure with the scales of contemplation.
This balance suggests that true justice requires both logic and fairness.
It is not about punishment, but about restoring equilibrium.
If the scales have tipped due to past actions, Justice appears to set them right, ensuring that the energy put out into the world returns to its source.
The Law of Consequence
Justice is the embodiment of Karma in its active form.
While the Wheel represents the turning of fate, Justice represents the specific consequences of our choices.
She teaches that every thought, word, and deed carries weight and creates a ripple in the fabric of reality.
She asks us to accept responsibility for our current circumstances, acknowledging that they are the harvest of seeds we planted long ago.
The Veil of Clarity
Behind her hangs a purple veil, signifying wisdom and the spiritual realm.
Unlike the High Priestess’s veil which hides mysteries, this veil serves as a backdrop, emphasizing her presence in the conscious world.
She stands between the pillars of duality, but unlike the Hierophant who interprets law for the masses, Justice demands that you internalize the law.
She requires you to judge yourself with honesty, stripping away the excuses and rationalizations of the ego.
An Invitation to Integrity
Drawing Justice is a call to align your actions with your values.
It asks you to seek the truth, even if it is uncomfortable, and to make decisions based on facts rather than emotions.
It invites you to act with integrity, knowing that you are always accountable to the high court of your own conscience.
It is a reminder that fairness begins within.
